transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Before we proceed with the share repurchase authorization, I'd like to hear from treasury, legal, and tax accounting on any relevant conditions I should be aware of. Let's start with treasury — do we have sufficient liquidity for the $6.1 million repurchase, and are there any working capital constraints we need to consider?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag an important constraint. Based on this morning's rolling cash forecast — which hasn't been circulated yet — the authorized repurchase amount we can actually pay while preserving the board-approved operating cash floor is $4,200,000. Importantly, this $4.2 million is the repurchase amount itself, not a total pool from which the excise-tax reserve would be deducted; the excise-tax reserve is booked separately. So the $6.1 million figure in the preliminary proposal would exceed what our cash position can support.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical legal constraint before Elena signs anything. While reviewing the corporate records this week, I found that the current board resolution requires this repurchase to be conducted through a Dutch auction — it may not use an open-market program. I have not yet updated the draft authorization to reflect this, so we need to ensure the execution method is specified as a Dutch auction before authorization is signed.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag a tax accounting condition before Elena signs the authorization. I confirmed in a tax memo received yesterday that this repurchase requires an excise-tax reserve of exactly $126,000 and a tax filing within 30 days after execution. The memo has not yet been added to the transaction file, so I wanted to make sure everyone is aware of these requirements before we proceed.
transcript.speaker: A4
